Suzukawa"The difference is where. The shogun has this authority in territory occupied through his campaigns. The Supreme Commander has it in regions judged necessary for a defensive war against an external enemy."

Suzukawa"Rokuhara did the same. 'We are in a time of national crisis.' Under this justification, it expanded its temporary emergency powers and claimed indefinite authority over all Yamato. The authority is temporary; only the ending has been removed."

en.html:
Regular visitors to this room could belong to two categories only. Outstanding students and outstanding headaches. Whichever end of the class you ran toward, principal sir was waiting. Safest position was somewhere in the middle, grazing quietly.

Me, I was standard-issue student. No outstanding anywhere. Naturally, first visit to the principal's office. I would like to report some great feeling, but no, nothing came. Even my first impression could not be bothered.

In a private academy for the little princes of high society, maybe. This was a public school. Where would one ordinary principal get an ebony desk and a pipe to sit smoking behind it? We had come for education, not to meet the last emperor of furniture.

One dry room, bas. If boredom needed accommodation, it could stay here. It would not even have to unpack.

The owner was also not a source of entertainment. What he had to say, toh, was entertainment's exact opposite.

I had guessed something of it on the way.

Forbidden was not quite right. GHQ was sitting there. Even Rokuhara could not ban its religion in front of its own face.

But the Shogunate had no warmth for Western culture, and Christianity was certainly not a favourite. Behind the scenes, I had heard, the persecution was severe.

So a government employee openly going to church—what would happen to him behind those same scenes?

Promotion ruk gaya, bas? Your career stops climbing and that is all?

Probably not that simple.

en.html:
Principal sir had to say yes.

Same thing he had been saying till just now.

But now yes was not coming. With Suzukawa in front of him, how would it come?

...Sach bolun, there was something unfair in the tactic.

Make a shield of your own suffering and force your demand through. If the other person caused that suffering, different matter. Otherwise, people would call it a low trick, and could you blame them? You were using the other person's conscience against him.

The violence of the weak.

But Suzukawa did not make a habit of this. His past, I had never once heard from his own mouth. This vow—I was hearing it for the first time today.

Maybe he had told nobody.

Then why now? Sympathy suddenly chahiye, is it? Surely not.

To help us.

ない。鈴川の過去も、おれは本人の口から聞いたこと
はこれまで一度もなかった。

　誓いのことは今日初めて知ったほどだ。
　おそらく、誰にも話したことがないのではないか。

　それを何故いま話したか、理由はまさか、急に人の
同情を買いたくなったからではないだろう。
　おれたちを助けるためだ。

en.html:
Nahin. Not just help.

Protect.

What he called beauty.

Something like that inside us? Honestly, the idea made me squirm. Sir had looked at the three of us and found beauty. I could barely find a useful reply inside myself. But for that thing he could see, he had swallowed his shame.

The shame of using that violence of the weak. And he did not seem like a man who could cover his own eyes and stop feeling it.

What that meant, I don't think I properly understood. Something was reaching me, haan. But the real weight of it? Probably not yet.

Still, one thing I had to do. Either apologise or thank him. One of those two.

Which one, yaar? Such a small selection, and still I was managing to get lost.

I did not know.

So I left the choosing alone and said what came.

　鈴川の云う美しさを。

　おれたちの中にそんなものがあるのかと考えれば、
正直くすぐったくなる。
　だがそのために、鈴川は恥を忍んだのだ。

いないと思う。

ないと思った。

　どちらか。
　わからなかった。

　わからなかったから、おれはとにかく自然に任せて
口にした。
